headline: Daily research brief — Friday, October 9

items.detail: Last night's inputs had MSFT near Nov 4 and AAPL near Oct 29 - both stale. TSLA (Oct 21 after close), MSFT (Oct 28 after close) and AAPL (Nov 2, announced) all now fall inside the 28-day option window. TSLA's Oct-23 straddle prices +/-7.5%, nearly identical to its 8-quarter average absolute reaction of 7.8% - fairly priced, no edge. Selling premium into any of the three is short gamma into a scheduled binary - avoid.

items.detail: NVDA is the only watchlist name with a clean read: 28-day IV 29.8% vs 24.5% realized (+22%, non-contingent window). The 28D-to-42D slope (29.8% to 35.0%) is the Nov-18 earnings premium on the back expiry - calendar mechanics, not fear. SPY is clean but modestly priced (12.2% vs 9.9%). QQQ's apparent richness is window-contingent (one September day drives 38.5% of its 20-day variance) - verdict withheld. No cheap or rich signal anywhere today.

items.detail: 2s10s at 47bp flattened 4bp on the day (10Y -6bp, 2Y -2bp); the curve is positive and not steep anywhere in the window. SOFR-EFFR sits at -1bp - no funding stress. The 60-day move is a parallel +50bp shift on both ends, which keeps equity risk premia thin and the margin-of-safety bar high for long-duration exposure (NVDA, TSLA, MSFT). Nothing in rates argues for widening liquidity-risk discounts.

items.detail: The October WASDE cut corn's bull case: yield raised to 181.2 bu/ac vs 177.7 expected, ending stocks 1.849B vs 1.67B - all three grains traded >1% lower. Hormuz tanker attacks are at their highest weekly rate since the war began, with crude transits at a 2-month low (-27% w/w). Hurricane Isaias makes landfall tonight with ~11.2M bbl of Gulf production at risk. Both benchmarks remain in steep backwardation - near-term physical tightness is real, not just paper fear.
